summary: Scheduler.run_all(delay_seconds=...) now sleeps only between jobs, not after the last one, so callers stop waiting for no reason. The fix is written, but memory shows no merge or release.
narrative: The owner opened with a small, specific ask: run_all(delay_seconds=...) slept after the last job as well, which wasted time. Memory records the diagnosis (observation 1) and a code change in schedule/__init__.py within about a minute (observation 2), so that sleep now happens only between jobs. Memory holds no PR, merge, release or owner confirmation, so the work is treated as built but not shipped.

milestones.text: Found that Scheduler.run_all sleeps after every job, including the last.
Changed run_all to sleep only between jobs.

preferences.preference: Likes small, wasteful-behaviour fixes taken first and stated precisely.
preferences.quote: Small one first: `run_all(delay_seconds=...)` also sleeps after the last job, which just wastes time.
